stories.headline: Earthquake of magnitude 4 struck China's Xinjiang
stories.title: Earthquake of magnitude 4 struck China's Xinjiang
stories.summary: Beijing , October 19 : A moderate earthquake of magnitude 4.0 on the Richter scale struck China’s Xinjiang region late Sunday night, according to the National Centre for Seismology. The seismic event occurred at 10:55 PM IST on October 18. According to the NCS, the epicentre was located at Latitude 36.683° N and Longitude 77.064° E. The earthquake originated at a depth of 190 kilometres beneath the Earth's surface, classifying it as an intermediate-to-deep focus quake. Due to the significant depth of the epicentre, surface tremors were likely muted across the region. In a post on X, NCS wrote, "EQ of M: 4.0, On: 18/10/2026 22:55:26 IST, Lat: 36.683 N, Long: 77.064 E, Depth: 190 Km, Location: Xinjiang." No immediate reports of casualties or major structural damage have been received. Local emergency management agencies are monitoring the situation. Earlier in July, an earthquake of magnitude 4.1 struck China on Saturday, according to the National Centre for Seismology (NCS). As per the NCS, the shallow earthquake occurred at a depth of 10 kilometres in the afternoon on July 4th. "EQ of M: 4.1, On: 04/07/2026 15:59:19 IST, Lat: 26.550 N, Long: 98.783 E, Depth: 10 km, Location: China," NCS said on X. It occurred near the border with Myanmar. Shallow earthquakes are generally more dangerous than deep earthquakes. This is because the seismic waves from shallow earthquakes have a shorter distance to travel to the surface, resulting in stronger ground shaking and potentially more damage to structures and greater casualties. China's geographical position makes it highly prone to frequent seismic activity. It is located between the two largest seismic belts, the circum-Pacific seismic belt and the circum-Indian seismic belt. Squeezed by the Pacific plate, the Indian plate and the Philippine plate, the seismic fracture zones are well developed in this region. Since the beginning of the 20th century, more than 800 earthquakes of magnitude 6 or greater have occurred in China. Earthquakes have struck almost all provinces, municipalities, and autonomous regions, except for Guizhou, Zhejiang, and Hong Kong. Since 1949, more than 100 destructive earthquakes have occurred across Chinese provinces, municipalities and autonomous regions, 14 of which are in East China. These earthquakes have caused the deaths of more than 2,70,000 people, representing 54 per cent of the total death toll caused by natural disasters in China. The earthquake-stricken districts cover an area of 3,00,000 square kilometres, with more than 7 million rooms destroyed. Experts note that earthquakes and other natural disasters continue to pose major challenges to China even in peaceful times.

stories.headline: Karnataka High Court Grants Bail To Pan Masala Manufacturer In Rs. 42 Crore Health Security & National Security Cess Evasion Case
stories.title: Karnataka High Court Grants Bail To Pan Masala Manufacturer In Rs. 42 Crore Health Security & National Security Cess Evasion Case
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'national security' in title weight 70
article_sentences: The Karnataka High Court has recently granted bail to S. Nithyananda-the proprietor of M/s N Square Enterprises-who was arrested under the newly enacted Health Security and National Security Cess (HSNS) Act, 202 for allegedly evading cess amounting to around 42 crores.
The single judge bench of Justice S Vishwajith Shetty granted him bail on October 17[Saturday].

The accused had been in judicial custody since August 20, 2026, following a crackdown by the Directorate General of GST Intelligence (DGGI), Bengaluru Zonal Unit at his factory in Nelamangala, and his residence in Sheshadripuram.

According to DGGI, the search of the factory led to the recovery of six undeclared vertical Forms, Fill and Seal (FFS) pouch packing machines, alongside large quantities of raw materials, packaging materials, and finished pan masala goods.

The department had earlier alleged that the accused was engaged in unregulated manufacture and clearance of pan masala, without following the norms for registration, declaration of machinery, or payment of applicable cess.
After the search, the DGGI computed the alleged evasion around Rs 1 crore per machine every month, with a total liability of around 42 crores for the time period of February 2026 -August 2026.

After his arrest, Nityananda had filed bail applications which were previously rejected by the Special Court for Economic Offences on September 1, and thereafter, the Sessions Court on October 6, 2026.
Senior Advocate Sunil Kumar S., appearing for the petitioner, argued that the entire case rests on a presumptive calculation of cess.
He heavily relied on the recent judgment of the High Court of Karnataka in M/s Dhariwal Industries Pvt.
Union of India, wherein a Single Judge bench of Justice M Nagaprasanna struck down the capacity-based manner of levying cess under the HSNS Act as violative of Article 14.
Though the Division Bench then subsequently stayed the single bench order, the petitioner contended that the liability to the tune of 42 crores attributed is a disputed departmental calculation.
Kumar argued that it should not be treated as a final adjudicated liability at the bail stage.

stories.headline: US missions in West Asia issue security alert over possible Iran-backed attacks
stories.title: US missions in West Asia issue security alert over possible Iran-backed attacks
stories.summary: Jerusalem, Oct 19: US missions across West Asia posted a security alert on Sunday advising their nationals to “exercise heightened vigilance,” citing Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia and the potential for Iran and its allied groups to launch attacks against American interests. “Be aware of potential flight cancellations, airspace closures, and travel disruptions,” the advisory said, adding that “the hostilities have the potential to escalate rapidly beyond that immediate area.” “Iran and groups supportive of Iran may target other US interests overseas or at locations associated with the United States and Americans throughout the world, including US businesses and other institutions,” the advisory said. The advisory came amid heightened security concerns in the region following drone and missile attacks by Yemen's Houthis on Saudi Arabia, including a deadly strike on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport on October 10 that killed 13 people, including an Indian national. The US views the Houthis as a key Iranian-backed armed group within Tehran’s regional network, with Iran providing weapons, funding and training, although the rebels retain considerable operational autonomy. US citizens travelling to or from West Asia were told to monitor information about airport and airline operations and develop contingency plans in advance. In view of the prevailing situation, the US embassy in Jerusalem also issued a list of “actions to be taken” and possible emergency assistance available. Fighting in Yemen has sharply escalated in October following the collapse of a multi-year informal cease-fire, with the Houthis launching major cross-border drone and missile strikes deep into Saudi Arabia. Yemen’s civil war erupted in 2014 when the Houthis seized the capital, Sanaa, and forced the internationally recognised government to relocate to Aden. Saudi Arabia led a military coalition into Yemen in March 2015 to support the government and push back against the Houthis, triggering years of fighting and airstrikes. A UN-brokered truce in 2022 brought a period of relative calm, followed by Saudi-Houthi talks aimed at securing a lasting settlement. However, the ceasefire was never formalised into a comprehensive peace agreement. The renewed Houthi escalation against Saudi Arabia adds a new regional dimension to the ongoing US-Iran conflict, threatening to widen hostilities beyond the immediate confrontation between Washington and Tehran. The conflict between the US and Iran, which started in February, remains locked in a military and diplomatic stalemate following the collapse of a June agreement. Iran continues to restrict shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, while the US maintains its naval port blockade on Tehran.

stories.headline: India-US trade deal close to being final; complex set of factors involved: Marco Rubio
stories.title: India-US trade deal close to being final; complex set of factors involved: Marco Rubio
stories.summary: The foreign policy of the US, of course, takes into account the war between Russia and Ukraine but it is not solely dominated by that, said Marco Rubio.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: India and the US are close to finalising the trade deal but the entire process involves a complex set of factors that are required to be taken into account, said US Secretary of State Marco Rubio ahead of his trip to India.
Rubio, who is in Uzbekistan now, will arrive in India on October 20.
He will meet External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar.
“We're trying to finalise a trade deal with India right now.
We're very close to doing that,” he told reporters on Monday.
He said the US has had to waive sanctions over the past few months because of the impact on global supplies and prices and the impact on other countries.
He said prices are high in the US but are “really, really high in a bunch of other countries”.
“We have to manage all of these things…Every country has a complex set of factors that it has to take into account.
Geography is real.
For some countries, it's very difficult to acquire energy from alternative sources.
That's not an excuse, but all of that has to be balanced when making foreign policy,” he said.

The foreign policy of the US, of course, takes into account the war between Russia and Ukraine but it is not solely dominated by that, it has to take into account a variety of factors including its bilateral relationships with other countries and what they are realistically capable of being able to do in terms of their own energy supplies, said Rubio.

stories.headline: Israeli PM Netanyahu warns of potentially hostile future US president, calls for alliances with India, Latin America
stories.title: Israeli PM Netanyahu warns of potentially hostile future US president, calls for alliances with India, Latin America
stories.summary: Jerusalem, Oct 19: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has warned that a future US president could be hostile towards Israel, calling for new alliances with countries such as India and those in Latin America to strengthen his country's position. Netanyahu made the remarks on Sunday during an event at which he presented his security doctrine, nine days before Israel's October 27 election. The remarks came hours before a strong endorsement he received from US President Donald Trump, who publicly expressed his support for Netanyahu's re-election bid days before the country goes to the polls. "In two years, a President, man or woman, could come to power who is very hostile to Israel," Netanyahu said. "How would you deal with that? How would you operate in relation to the United States? And beyond that, what solutions would be necessary?", he questioned. The Israeli Premier stressed that Israel must use the remaining years of Trump's presidency to strengthen its position while preparing for a potentially dramatic shift in American policy. "First, we must do everything we can during these two years, and during the following two years, in the American arena, through good times and bad," he said. "The second thing is to create other alliances. That is what I am working on now with many countries in our region and outside it. India is not a small country, and there are many others," the Israeli Prime Minister emphasised. He pointed to political developments in Latin America as another opportunity to expand Israel's network of allies. "There is a major shift in Latin America, and there could be an enormous change in Brazil in just a few days," Netanyahu pointed out, adding, "We must expand our pool of alliances and develop capabilities that make us valuable to everyone." Netanyahu has often evoked India and his relationship with Prime Minister Narendra Modi to argue that Israel is not isolated globally and to demonstrate his government's diplomatic successes. Countering issues of delegitimisation and alliances amid a prolonged war, Netanyahu, in May this year, in a much publicised statement, said that his country enjoys a "unique relationship" with "huge power" India where there is "crazy love" for Israel. Many analysts in Israel feel that the growing apathy among Democrats in the US results from poor choices Netanyahu made over the years. His relations with Democratic Party-led Presidents Barack Obama and Joe Biden were often tense, which he presented to his supporters as the courage of a strong leader willing to stand up against American Presidents to safeguard Israel's interests, the analysts believe. This has been a cornerstone of Netanyahu's election campaigns and a recipe for electoral success, they said. He is Israel's longest-serving Prime Minister. Gadi Eisenkot, the main challenger to the Israeli Prime Minister in the upcoming polls, sharply criticised the presentation, describing it as an empty political exercise rather than a serious national security strategy. "Nine days before the election and three years after the gravest failure and disaster in Israel's history, with every war front still open, Netanyahu decided to present his 'security doctrine' to the public," Eisenkot said. "Two hollow pages, full of slogans that have nothing whatsoever to do with a security doctrine, reveal more than anything the strategic vacuum Netanyahu has left the State of Israel in and his disregard for the security of Israeli citizens," he asserted. Eisenkot, a former Chief of Staff of the Israel Defence Forces, accused Netanyahu of attempting to manipulate public opinion and spread fear ahead of the election. "This is Netanyahu's method: manipulating perceptions, frightening people and trying to divert attention from the parade of lies and racism surrounding his campaign tonight," he said.

stories.headline: Supreme Court cancels patta on Tamil Nadu water body, protects flat owners
stories.title: Supreme Court cancels patta on Tamil Nadu water body, protects flat owners
stories.summary: Supreme Court cancels patta on Tamil Nadu water body, protects flat owners
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: The Supreme Court upheld the cancellation of a patta covering government water body land.
Tamil Nadu must allot alternative land to 20 flat owners before demolition.
The Supreme Court has upheld the cancellation of a ‘ryotwari patta’ granted for land recorded as a government water body in Tamil Nadu, news agency Press Trust of India reported.

A bench of Justices SVN Bhatti and NV Anjaria, in its judgment delivered on October 16, directed the state government to allot a suitable alternative site to the owners of 20 flats before demolishing their apartments.

A ‘ryotwari patta’ is an official revenue and land record issued to an individual cultivator, certifying the right to occupy and cultivate a specific piece of land while paying land tax directly to the government.
Justice Bhatti, who wrote the judgment for the bench, said the flat owners were led to believe, because of official orders and revenue records, that the state government had no interest in the land.

“Therefore, directing the demolition of flats without examining the hardship of the flat owners and the independent remedies available to them in law against the owner of the land and the developer of the apartments would cause irreparable financial injury and throw the families on the streets,” the bench said.

“In the circumstances of the case, to ameliorate the possible hardship and, without committing a breach of Section 14-A of the Tamil Nadu Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948, we direct the Chief Secretary, State of Tamil Nadu, and the District Collector, Tiruvallur, to allot a vacant, commensurate site to the owners of the flats represented by the Society, preferably within 6 months from today, and thereafter to undertake the demolition of the constructed area to an extent of 0.22 acres,” it added.
According to PTI, the verdict dismissed three civil appeals filed by a flat owner and Tamil Nadu Mercantile Bank Ltd.
The appeals challenged the cancellation of the patta and subsequent directions to restore the land as a water body.
The case concerned land under a particular survey number at Thirumullaivoyal village in Tiruvallur district.
It was recorded in the 1911 resettlement register as “Government Poramboke – Kanakkan Kuttai”.

stories.headline: HERC Grants Parallel Distribution Licence to Eleven Power for Gurugram, Nuh
stories.title: HERC Grants Parallel Distribution Licence to Eleven Power for Gurugram, Nuh
stories.summary: The Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission (HERC) has granted Eleven Power Private Limited a 25-year parallel electricity distribution licence for Gurugram and Nuh, allowing consumers in the two districts to choose between the company and the existing distribution licensee as its network expands. The licence, granted through an order under Section 14 of the Electricity Act, 2003, marks the first parallel distribution licence in Haryana, according to the company. Eleven Power said the licence covers more than 8.3 lakh electricity consumers across residential, agricultural, commercial and industrial categories. The grant introduces the prospect of competition in electricity distribution in the two districts, although consumers will be able to switch only as Eleven Power’s network reaches their respective areas. The existing distribution licensee will continue to supply its consumers, and no immediate action is required from them, the company said. stories.headline: Pinarayi Vijayan's link emerges in controversial KIIFB land acquisition in Kannur
stories.title: Pinarayi Vijayan's link emerges in controversial KIIFB land acquisition in Kannur
stories.summary: Pinarayi Vijayan faces scrutiny over KIIFB land acquisition in Kannur amid allegations of irregularities, high land prices, delayed compensation and stalled industrial projects in Kerala.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Pinarayi Vijayan faces scrutiny over KIIFB land acquisition in Kannur amid allegations of irregularities, high land prices, delayed compensation and stalled industrial projects in Kerala.

Thiruvananthapuram: Information has now surfaced that former Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan had called for the urgent acquisition of land in Kannur through the Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Board (KIIFB), stressing its necessity for industrial development.
Vijayan, when he led (2016-26) Kerala, pressed for the acquisition during a meeting with the KIIFB chief executive officer, maintaining that the land was essential for industrial development.
The disclosure assumes significance amid allegations of serious irregularities in the acquisition and questions over the high prices paid for the land.
Kerala Industrial Infrastructure Development Corporation (KINFRA) reportedly fixed the price at Rs 2.5 crore per acre in Kannur and Rs 1 crore per acre in Palakkad.

This came out last week when the details of the expert committee headed by former Finance Secretary Sudha Pillai flagged serious irregularities in KIIFB’s land acquisitions during the previous LDF government.
The committee raised concerns over purchases at prices reportedly as high as five times the market value.

Despite the substantial outlay and the stated urgency of the industrial projects, no work has begun on the Kannur land so far, raising questions over the justification for the acquisition and the delay in putting the property to use.
The issue has also left hundreds of small landowners in distress.
More than 700 acres in two villages in Kannur were notified for acquisition around eight years ago, but the affected owners were yet to receive compensation.
They say they cannot mortgage the land to secure loans or cultivate it.
Even new drinking water connections to their homes have reportedly become difficult to obtain because of the acquisition notification.

stories.headline: Jio Platforms’ relative valuation reasonable with headroom left on phone tariffs
stories.title: Jio Platforms’ relative valuation reasonable with headroom left on phone tariffs
stories.summary: On pricing, Jio holds promise when viewed purely as a telecom company.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Can Jio Platforms’ initial public offering (IPO) break the jinx of largely disappointing mega issues such as Hyundai Motor India and the National Stock Exchange of India?
Well, for the sake of Reliance Retail’s expected IPO over the next couple of years, it is critical that Jio’s IPO is successful.
Let's first look at the pricing.
Jio holds promise when viewed purely as a telecom company.
At the upper end of its price band of ₹1,065-1,119 apiece, the size of ₹30,213 crore will make it the biggest public issue in India’s capital market history.

Jio’s annualized FY27 EPS (earnings per share) could be about ₹35, based on the June quarter (Q1FY27) results, after factoring in a 3% rise in the number of equity shares post-issue, which means a price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple of 32 at ₹1,119.
On FY28 estimates, the P/E could be lower if Jio decides to improve average revenue per user (Arpu) instead of focusing on garnering more customers.
Over the past four years to FY26, Jio added 92 million subscribers for a total of 497 million, almost twice the number added by Bharti Airtel even as the latter’s Arpu has grown faster.
Jio has used pricing to capture most of the incremental users.
However, mobile penetration in India has saturated, with QoQ subscriber growth for Jio and Airtel moderating to about 1% in Q1.
So, Jio can think of increasing prices.
Jio’s mobile Arpu in FY26 was ₹203 versus Airtel’s ₹254.

stories.title: Odisha Issues Consultancy Tender for 225 MW Floating Solar + BESS Project
stories.summary: Grid Corporation of Odisha (GRIDCO), a state owned PSU and the nodal agency has sought bids for undertaking an impact study for developing floating solar projects across the states, seeking Expression of Interests ( EoIs) till November 17, 2026 Through this tender, the developers are required to select solar developers to develop, operate and maintain three units of grid-connected floating solar photovoltaic (FSPV) projects of 75 MW each, collectively, aggregating to 225 MW. Combined with a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS), together this project aims to supply power to GRIDCO . GRIDCO through the latest consultancy tender requires the bidders to act as the solar park developer for developing solar park over the Upper Indravati reservoir (Upper Indravati Solar Park) under its renewable energy Renewable Energy Policy. Scope of Work Under the scope of work, the developer is expected to undertake the Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) , and prepare E&S with IFC's Environmental and Social Performance Standards (2012). The deliverables include the Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA), Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP), Occupational Health Safety (OHS) plan and associated management instruments including the Livelihood Restoration Plan (LRP), Indigenous Peoples Development Plan (IPDP), Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP), and Grievance Mechanism (GM). A Livelihood Restoration Framework (LRF) and Stakeholder Engagement Framework (SEF) have been prepared at the scoping stage. The ESIA Consultant would be based on detailed impact assessment and identification of affected persons, prepare a Livelihood Restoration Plan (LRP) as part of the ESIA/ESMP documentation in accordance with the LRF Project Components Footprint The core AOI includes all areas directly occupied or physically disturbed by the Project components and associated facilities: The Floating Solar Photovoltaic ( FSPV ) project would be installed over the Indravati Reservoir (~6.5 sq. km) with a 33 kV transmission line and associated buffer. Launching pad, temporary storage areas. The developer would also have to build a Power Substation (PSS), Right of Way ( RoW ) for the 220 kV transmission line up to Mukhiguda Grid Substation. The Reservoir area within Floating solar project area, where direct aquatic ecological impacts are anticipated. The scope of work covers 15 villages comprising of 8 project villages and 7 AoI villages) These areas are anticipated to experience direct environmental and social interactions associated with the Project. Project footprint included within the following villages. The floating solar project is at Padepadar, Gaura Kurumuli and Paraja Kurumuli. The transmission Line would connect Padepadar, Uparchobari, Podapadar, Tikilipadar, Mahulpatna, Kamaridhi Scope of the Study: The developer is required ti review all existing project information and establish a baseline for climate and hydrological conditions. This includes an initial narrative review of all available documents and datasets to understand the project context, technical design considerations, and reservoir-dam operating environment. The following key documents and datasets will be collected and reviewed. The Project design reports and layout plans. It would be required to manage Bathymetry data, reservoir characteristics, and dam technical information and also develop Hydrological studies prepared as part of the project’s technical design.
